text:
Connor Hellebuyck has spent his first month in New Jersey carrying more than a goalie's usual load. He asked out of Winnipeg, sat out training camp, was traded to the Devils on Oct. 23, and has since said the threats against his family went beyond online death threats. On the ice it has been uneven lately: pulled after a disastrous first period in a 9-6 loss in St. Louis on Saturday, then steady again in Monday's 3-2 win over these same Blue Jackets. This season he sits at -0.7 goals saved above expected, which is to say about average.

That matters because the Devils skaters are doing their part. They take 57% of the expected goals at five on five (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and their +15 goal difference trails a +23.0 expected one. Our numbers say the goaltending has cost them 9.6 goals so far. They are second in the Metropolitan and at 95% to make the playoffs, and they're doing it without Anthony Mantha (neck, out until around Dec. 17) and Johnathan Kovacevic. Timo Meier has goals in four straight games, and Evan Rodrigues, our sleeper tonight at 17% to score, has 8 points in his last ten with the chances to back it up.

Columbus is the opposite story: a team that has been better than its record. A -17 goal difference sits on -8.8 expected, with 9.6 fewer goals than its chances usually produce. Matthew Knies, traded from Toronto on the eve of the season, just had his emotional return to Scotiabank Arena and a win to go with it. Zach Werenski has 11 points in ten and a five-game point streak. Cam Talbot, at +5.3 saved above expected, has been the reason the Jackets aren't further back. They're seventh in the division and at 8% for the playoffs. Sean Monahan is off the out list and day-to-day.

Our numbers have the Devils at 3.38 expected goals to Columbus's 2.82, and Monday's meeting was one New Jersey deserved to win 64% of the time.
headline: Hellebuyck and the Devils get Columbus again, two days later
